answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the sonnet check immediately, the harbor audit keeps the resolved set and the comet replay shows exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 198 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 198 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
